facts.text: Lonaconing sits in the Georges Creek Valley and was founded by late 18th century settlers like VanBuskirk and Dye.
The town once hosted a blast furnace operated by the Georges Creek Coal and Iron Company from 1836 to 1855, a relic of its mining past.
In 1973 the Lonaconing Furnace earned a spot on the National Register of Historic Places, preserving its industrial heritage.
The Georges Creek Railroad, built in 1851, linked Lonaconing southward to the B&O at Piedmont, later absorbed by the Cumberland and Pennsylvania Railroad by 1870.
Baseball legend Lefty Grove, a Hall of Fame pitcher, was born in Lonaconing, and his 1941 MVP trophy hangs in the local library.
The town’s historic district was added to the National Register in 1983, showcasing its well-preserved 19th‑century architecture.
